lines.text: About 90% of America's money was never printed.
lines.say: About ninety percent of America's money was never printed.

lines.text: In August 2026, cash was $2.39 trillion. The money supply, M2, was $23.34 trillion. Cash is only about 10%.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-six, cash was two point three nine trillion dollars. The money supply, called M two, was twenty-three point three four trillion. Cash is only about ten percent.

lines.text: Most of the rest is bank deposits. And banks create deposits when they lend.
lines.say: Most of the rest is bank deposits. And banks create deposits when they lend.

lines.text: Not a conspiracy theory: the Bank of England spelled it out in 2014.

lines.text: Say a bank lends you $20,000 for a car. It doesn't hand over someone's savings. It creates a new $20,000 deposit.
lines.say: Say a bank lends you twenty thousand dollars for a car. It doesn't hand over someone's savings. It creates a brand-new twenty thousand dollar deposit.

lines.text: And when you pay the loan back, that money disappears again.
lines.say: And when you pay the loan back, that money disappears again.

lines.text: Since March 2020, the Fed's reserve requirement has been zero.
lines.say: Since March twenty twenty, the Fed's reserve requirement has been zero.

lines.text: So what stops banks? Capital rules, borrowers who can repay, and interest rates.
lines.say: So what stops banks? Capital rules, borrowers who can actually repay, and interest rates.

lines.text: Your loan isn't just borrowed money. It's brand-new money.

post.title: About 90% of US money was never printed. Banks made it
post.ig:
About 90% of America's money was never printed.

August 2026: currency $2.39 trillion, M2 money supply $23.34 trillion (Fed).
Most of the rest is bank deposits, and banks create deposits when they lend (Bank of England, 2014).
A $20,000 loan creates a new $20,000 deposit. Repay it, and it disappears.
The Fed's reserve requirement has been 0% since March 2020.

Sources: Federal Reserve H.6 (Sept 2026), Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1.
